key_insight: Optimized gradient boosting predicted tensile strength of friction stir-welded 7N01 aluminum alloy with R² = 0.978 and mapped welding conditions targeting at least 90% joint efficiency.
engineering_relevance: The model provides a quantitative basis for selecting welding parameters, with shoulder plunge depth helping refine the predicted high-strength process window.
method: Predict ultimate tensile strength from rotational speed, welding speed, and shoulder plunge depth.
Compare baseline models, then tune gradient boosting decision trees using grid search.
Use SHAP to interpret parameter effects and identify feasible welding windows.
evidence_signal: Using 27 experimental samples and leave-one-out cross-validation, the study reports R² improving from 0.905 for a decision tree to 0.966 for gradient boosting and 0.978 after tuning.
watch_item: The small dataset limits confidence in generalization; predicted process windows need independent experimental validation before production use.
paper_title: Interpretable ensemble learning for tensile strength prediction and welding process window optimization of friction stir-welded 7N01 aluminum alloy
